correctness.rationale: The \(q\)-Frobenius orbit of a root has length exactly \(p\), giving \(q/p\) distinct degree-\(p\) factors. The finite-field reciprocal-sum identity and the normalized finite-difference bijection give \(T_m(b+a)=T_m(b)-T_{m-1}(b)\); Pascal induction yields \(T_m(na)=(-1)^m\binom nm\), hence \((1-X)^n\). The standard even-character reduction then gives \(\deg g=n-1\). Distinct \(a\) give disjoint factor sets. The inspected verifier checks the genuinely nonprime case \(q=25\) exactly.

evidence: Anglès supplies the framework but not this counterexample family; Giraudin supplies the family only for \(q=p\).

originality.rationale: Giraudin's full paper explicitly assumes \(q=p\) prime. The audited result treats arbitrary prime-power base size, where \(U^q-U-a\) is reducible and needs a new factor-orbit analysis and \(\mathbb F_q\) recursion. No prior prime-power extension was found.

source_inspections.title: An infinite family of counterexamples to Goss's conjecture on L-functions of cyclotomic function fields

value.rationale: Extending the new counterexample mechanism from prime fields to every prime-power base is structurally nontrivial because irreducibility fails; the exact factor count makes the extension quantitatively useful.

final_claim: For \(q=p^s\), \(p\ge5\), every degree-\(p\) factor \(P\) of \(U^q-U-a\), \(a\ne0\), and \(1\le n\le p-1\), one has \(D_{P,q^n-1}(X)=(1-X)^n\) and \(\deg_X g=n-1\); for \(3\le n\le p-1\) the construction supplies exactly \(q(q-1)/p\) degree-\(p\) counterexample primes.
limitations: Specific Artin--Schreier family and magic indices \(q^n-1\) only.
The prime count is only for this construction.
